decisions: Read canonical Schima2020 ordinals4,7,9,22,24,37,39,43,44, including surrounding passage context. This is a narrative review, not a new diagnostic-accuracy study.
Focal enlargement is a mass-forming pattern, not a numerical pancreas-head size cutoff. CP occasionally shows this pattern; pancreatic head location also overlaps PDAC.
MFCP/PDAC requires combined findings; no single reliable discriminator. This source limitation stays with both MFCP records. Do not broaden PDAC to all pancreatic tumors.
Duct-penetrating sign strongly favors an inflammatory mass but does not establish a diagnosis; method is MRCP. Omit the cited94percent accuracy because its population/denominator are not curated.
Calcification combination uses parenchymal OR ductal calcification, not a requirement for both. Tissue is a plain-language paraphrase of parenchymal.
Complete duct obstruction and arterial encasement by a soft-tissue mass are more likely in PDAC in this comparison; these do not diagnose a current scan.

Focal AIP homogeneous enhancement is portal-venous phase CT, not every phase or all inflammation. Retain smooth duct/no abrupt cutoff, mild upstream main duct dilatation≤5mm and absent proximal atrophy as a cluster. The5mm figure concerns the duct, not head/lesion diameter.
AIP overlap comes from ordinal43, not misapplied MFCP-specific single-feature evidence. No AIP exclusion rule or diagnostic certainty inferred.
Patient diagnosis and numerical head-size threshold exclusions are application policy, labeled separately from source claims. No assessment of the user scan, treatment or probability.

Records contain reusable source relations and structured comparison scope; no question text, expected answers or evaluation labels. Engineering review binds this interpretation but does not prove it or count as independent/human acceptance.
